</mxCell> <mxCell id="notes" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;fontFamily=Arial;fontSize=13;fontColor=#232F3E;align=left;verticalAlign=top;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;spacing=0;" value="<b style="font-size:16px">Legend</b><ol style="padding-left:20px;margin-top:10px;margin-bottom:10px"><li style="margin-bottom:6px"><b>Nigerian customers</b> reach <b>core banking</b> in the primary Lagos data centre.</li><li style="margin-bottom:6px">Core banking and the <b>customer database</b> share a site, so the round trip stays under 5 ms. No cloud Region can: Lagos to Cape Town is about 4,800 km, at least 48 ms there and back in fibre.</li><li style="margin-bottom:6px">Every transaction is written to an on-premises <b>WORM audit store</b>, so logs that contain personal data never leave Nigeria.</li><li style="margin-bottom:6px">The database replicates to a <b>secondary data centre in Nigeria</b>. Data stays on <b>EBS</b> in Lagos, with no snapshots.</li><li style="margin-bottom:6px"><b>EU customers and EU fintech partners</b> call <b>Amazon API Gateway</b> in eu-west-1. Partner APIs that carry Nigerian data end in the Lagos data centre instead.</li><li style="margin-bottom:6px">EU services on <b>AWS Fargate</b> keep EU personal data in <b>Amazon RDS</b> in a private subnet (GDPR).</li><li style="margin-bottom:6px">Audit events go to <b>Amazon S3</b> with Object Lock in compliance mode, so no one can alter or delete them.</li></ol><b>Residency rule:</b><ul style="padding-left:20px;margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:10px"><li style="margin-bottom:6px">Nigerian personal data, its backups and its logs stay in Nigeria.</li><li style="margin-bottom:6px">Only anonymised aggregates cross to eu-west-1.</li></ul><b>Identity:</b><ul style="padding-left:20px;margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:10px"><li style="margin-bottom:6px">One public cloud. <b>IAM Identity Center</b> federates with the bank's on-premises directory, so there is one source of identities.</li></ul><b>Cost:</b><ul style="padding-left:20px;margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:10px"><li style="margin-bottom:6px">GPUs run on demand, so nothing idles between training runs.</li><li style="margin-bottom:6px">Option: <b>AWS Outposts</b> racks, available in Nigeria, bring AWS APIs on premises.</li></ul>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="880" width="360" x="1500" y="120" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div:
Regulated bank: hybrid deployment
Where each workload runs, and how Nigerian data stays in Nigeria

text.tspan: Where each workload runs, and how Nigerian data stays in Nigeria

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 362px; height: 1px; padding-top: 121px; margin-left: 1500px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #232F3E;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Arial; color: #232F3E; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

ol.li: Nigerian customers reach core banking in the primary Lagos data centre.
Core banking and the customer database share a site, so the round trip stays under 5 ms. No cloud Region can: Lagos to Cape Town is about 4,800 km, at least 48 ms there and back in fibre.
Every transaction is written to an on-premises WORM audit store, so logs that contain personal data never leave Nigeria.
The database replicates to a secondary data centre in Nigeria. Automated failover meets the 15-minute recovery time without moving data abroad.
AI training on Nigerian data bursts to GPU instances in the AWS Lagos Local Zone over AWS Direct Connect. Data stays on EBS in Lagos, with no snapshots.
EU customers and EU fintech partners call Amazon API Gateway in eu-west-1. Partner APIs that carry Nigerian data end in the Lagos data centre instead.
EU services on AWS Fargate keep EU personal data in Amazon RDS in a private subnet (GDPR).
Audit events go to Amazon S3 with Object Lock in compliance mode, so no one can alter or delete them.

ul.li: Nigerian personal data, its backups and its logs stay in Nigeria.
Only anonymised aggregates cross to eu-west-1.
One public cloud. IAM Identity Center federates with the bank's on-premises directory, so there is one source of identities.
GPUs run on demand, so nothing idles between training runs.
Option: AWS Outposts racks, available in Nigeria, bring AWS APIs on premises.
